props.title: Long-term habits
props.sub: Start early, learn continuously, own mistakes, and keep money in perspective.

props.big: Starting with a small, sustainable amount can give learning and compounding more time to work.
props.sub: Do not confuse the power of time with a promise of any future return.

props.title: Skill compounds when outcomes become feedback instead of blame
props.note: Keep an investment journal: thesis, valuation, risks, and what later proved wrong.

props.big: The author's lesson is to begin learning and investing with a manageable amount, because time is useful only when paired with survival and discipline.
props.sub: The book's future-value illustration is historical and not a return promise.

props.big: In markets, popularity can be a signal to investigate expectations, not a reason to abandon independent analysis.
props.sub: Contrarian thinking means evidence-led independence, not automatically doing the opposite of everyone else.

props.big: Review losses for errors in process, research, position size, or behaviour instead of outsourcing blame to a broker, adviser, or market.
props.sub: Taking responsibility is how an investor turns a loss into a process improvement.

props.big: The author's interpersonal lesson is to evaluate people and processes fairly, especially during difficult periods.
props.sub: For investing, this means disciplined review rather than emotional praise or condemnation after a short result.

props.big: The final lesson is that financial success should support a healthy, meaningful life — not become its only measure.
props.sub: Good investing serves life goals; it should not consume judgment, relationships, or well-being.

props.title: A calmer way to invest
items: Treat shares as ownership claims, not tips or lottery tickets.
Protect capital with knowledge, balance-sheet discipline, and position limits.
Judge business quality, management incentives, and valuation together.
Buy and sell from a written thesis, never from an entry-price anchor.
Diversify by economic exposure; use screens only to begin research.
Verify advisers and reject guaranteed-return claims.
Keep learning, own mistakes, and let time do its work.
props.closer: Information from a 2017 educational book; not investment advice. Consult a SEBI-registered adviser for personal decisions.
